content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the disease symptoms.

The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Mosaic/mottled pattern (light green and yellow-green areas interspersed with darker green)
- Leaf distortion/puckering/wrinkling
- No distinct necrotic spots or lesions
- Bumpy, rough leaf texture

This pattern strongly suggests a viral disease. Top candidates are **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus** or **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**. Let me check reference images.
This CMV reference shows whole plant wilting. Let me check Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus next.
TSWV shows dark/bronze spotting — doesn't match. Let me check another CMV reference showing leaf-level symptoms.
This CMV reference (Bugwood_4.jpg) shows the same leaf distortion and puckering pattern I see in the test image. Let me use my final view on Early_Blight to rule it out.

Early Blight shows necrotic brown spots — clearly different from the test image.

**Summary of findings:**
- **Test image**: Tomato leaf with mosaic/mottled pattern (yellow-green patches + darker green areas), leaf puckering/distortion, bumpy texture, no discrete necrotic lesions
- **CMV (Bugwood_4.jpg)**: Matches — shows same leaf distortion, puckering, and mosaic mottling pattern
- **TSWV**: Ruled out — shows dark bronze spotting and necrotic marks, not mosaic mottling
- **Early Blight**: Ruled out — shows distinct brown necrotic lesions and yellowing halos

The mosaic color pattern + leaf distortion/puckering with no discrete lesions is the hallmark of Cucumber Mosaic Virus infection.
